subject.title: memory index: openclaw memory index --force exits early without processing full backlog, no error logged

question: Is the current-main status-denominator fix enough to close this report, or should this issue stay open until maintainers get live proof for the reported large Gemini `memory index --force` early-exit/no-error path?
rationale: The merged denominator work explains one visible backlog mismatch, but it does not prove the reporter's manual forced-index run now drains the real corpus or fails loudly.

options.title: Keep open for live force-index proof
options.body: Keep this issue as the tracker for the remaining large-corpus forced-index symptom and require a current-main or next-release live repro before opening a new fix PR.

options.title: Close after denominator release
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide the status-denominator mismatch fully explains the user's observed backlog and no broader `--force` failure needs tracking.

options.title: Split a provider-specific follow-up
options.body: Close this issue only after opening a narrower follow-up with Gemini/provider logs, current-main status output, and exact dirty-session counts.

recommendation.title: Keep open for live force-index proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the tracker for the remaining large-corpus forced-index symptom and require a current-main or next-release live repro before opening a new fix PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory reindex and release-carrying history makes this the best available routing candidate for the proof-sufficiency decision.
